title: Depression: screening, first-line drugs, and what to do when they fail

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on USPSTF screening guidance and the APA major depressive disorder guideline. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: From what PHQ-9 score is depression considered at least moderate?
questions.why: The bands are 5, 10, 15 and 20 for mild, moderate, moderately severe and severe. The last item, on thoughts of being better off dead, is checked at every visit.

questions.q: Before starting an antidepressant, which history must be asked about specifically?
questions.a: Past episodes of mania or hypomania
questions.why: An antidepressant alone can precipitate mania in bipolar disorder. A history of elevated mood, reduced need for sleep or reckless spending changes the whole plan.

questions.q: Which are reasonable first-line antidepressants for a first episode of moderate depression?
questions.why: Tricyclics and MAOIs work but carry overdose and interaction risks that keep them second line. Psychotherapy is an equal first-line option, and the combination beats either alone.

questions.q: How long is an adequate trial of an antidepressant at a therapeutic dose before judging it a failure?
questions.why: Some response is usually visible by 2 to 4 weeks, and none at all by then predicts a poor outcome, which is when a dose increase is considered.

questions.q: After remission of a first episode, how long should the antidepressant be continued?
questions.why: After three or more episodes, or a severe or suicidal episode, maintenance is long term. Stopping at the first good week is the commonest cause of relapse.

questions.q: A patient has a partial response after eight weeks of sertraline at a good dose. Which strategy fits?
questions.a: Augment, for example with bupropion or an atypical antipsychotic
d: Stop sertraline and start a different SSRI
Double the dose beyond the licensed maximum
questions.why: No response points to switching; partial response points to augmenting or adding psychotherapy. Lithium and thyroid hormone are older augmentation options.

questions.q: Which antidepressant should be avoided in a patient with a seizure disorder or an eating disorder?
questions.why: It lowers the seizure threshold, more so with purging and electrolyte loss. Its advantage elsewhere is no sexual dysfunction and no weight gain.

questions.q: An older patient on an SSRI develops confusion. Which laboratory abnormality is the SSRI most likely to have caused?
questions.why: SSRIs cause SIADH, especially in the first weeks and in older women. They also raise bleeding risk with NSAIDs and anticoagulants.

questions.q: Which drugs raise the risk of serotonin syndrome when combined with an SSRI?
questions.why: Triptans and dextromethorphan are lesser contributors. The picture is agitation, clonus, hyperreflexia, tremor and fever within hours of the combination.

questions.q: Which antidepressants cause the worst discontinuation symptoms when stopped abruptly?
questions.why: Both have short half-lives. Fluoxetine's long half-life makes it the one that can be stopped without a taper, and the one sometimes used to bridge a taper.

questions.q: A 19-year-old is starting an SSRI. What does the boxed warning about suicidality change in practice?
questions.a: Closer follow-up in the first weeks, not withholding treatment
d: No SSRI can be prescribed under 25
questions.why: Untreated depression is the larger suicide risk. The usual pattern is a visit or call within one to two weeks of starting and again after any dose change.

questions.q: Which antidepressant is usually preferred for a breastfeeding mother with postpartum depression?
questions.why: It passes into milk in the smallest amounts of the SSRIs and has the most safety data. Fluoxetine's long half-life makes it accumulate in the infant.
